title: Capital Budget Selection

statement.md: A desk has a risk budget $W$. There are $n$ candidate positions, each with a risk weight $w_i$ and an expected value $v_i$. Choose a subset of positions, each at most once, whose total weight is at most $W$ and whose total value is as large as possible.

inputFormat: First line: $n$ and $W$. Then $n$ lines `w v`.
hints: Define $f(i, c)$ as the best value using the first $i$ positions with capacity $c$. What are the two choices for position $i$?
If you keep only one row of the table, which direction must the capacity loop run so an item is not used twice?
editorial: [{"type": "p", "md": "The recurrence is $f(i, c) = \\max(f(i-1, c),\\; f(i-1, c - w_i) + v_i)$ when $c \\ge w_i$, with $f(0, c) = 0$. One row is enough if the capacity loop runs from high to low, because each cell then still reads the previous item layer. Time $O(nW)$, memory $O(W)$. Looping upward would allow reusing the same item."}]
